reviews.review: Is not a pleasant game for me. Fighting mechanics are sluggish and unresponsive with so so aiming. Journey progression is locked on linear (if you shoot a bow without being in the archer journey, you don't get the bow shooting journey step). Forget about a fun archer class, the arrows do very little dmg in pve (apparently good in pvp according to reddit i think though but haven't tried) but weight a ton (I suppose you could get expertise to carry more but that makes you miss out on skills necessary for a viable archer). There is an infinite arrow bow but the penalties are too high to make it interesting.

I love this game.
Been playing this game for more than 4,500 hours (PvE, solo).
This review is aimed at the changes in the Enhanced version, not the game in general.
TL;DR: Superficially nice, but it offers nothing the legacy version doesn't have. 
(UI Slider?!? devs, hello?)

I stayed with the legacy version for a long time because I hesitated to set up my modlist every time they release a new engine update. Now I decided to make the switch a few days ago, but I am not excited about the Enhanced version at all.

The new graphics look really nice, but that's it. The shadows and lighting create an uncomfortable environment that is almost painful to play in for longer than a few minutes. It looks nice in the trailers, but actual gameplay is more than uncomfortable.

Worst of all is the UI. Everything in the HUD is way too small, except the Journey steps, which obscure half of the screen. On the other hand, everything in the Inventory and Knowledge tabs is HUGE. The icons are way too big, making the whole interface feel almost claustrophobic. It feels like a lazy mobile or console layout forced onto Pc players.

WHY is there no UI size slider?
I'll never understand how in the world game developers can basically create a new version of a game but completely ignore such a crucial element like the UI. Even worse, they didn't include any UI scaling whatsoever, leaving PC players completely stranded. 

EDIT: I almost forgot. Why does the camera zoom in and out like crazy when i have target lock activated? What in the world is this supposed to archieve? The only thing it causes is motion sickness. 
(Keep it as it was before. IT WAS FINE!!)

I have no idea what's going on with the devs of this game, but these things are the OPPOSITE of improvements. THIS is why i do not recommend the game.

Fantastic exploration, visuals and sound design. Whoever they got working on sound effects needs a promotion and payrise, the sound in this game is amazing (I played with headphones). The game doesn't hold your hand and you have to read and interpret what the game expects you to do next, which is something I enjoy. You could call it a discount Elden Ring. There is a story but you have to go hunting for it and piece it all together. There is very little guidance. 

The bad is the combat is undercooked. All weapons feel the same except for having different armor penetration values, which makes the mace/hammer hands down best for everything because it has the highest armor pen. I tried switching to various other weapons but they purely underperformed. The hitboxes are bad and you have to basically hug enemies to be able to hit them which makes the spear with its range pointless. 

Whoever decided you couldn't repair legendary gear needs to be fired and replaced by the sound design guy, I reckon he can do a better job balancing gear and combat in this game. Yes I'm aware they added some smithy but I'm not slogging through some dungeon to repair gear. Its like they made things arbitrarily difficult to deter you from gearing yourself. Which leads to my next point.

Thralls/Companions are 4-5 times more effective at combat damage than you are because you end up gearing them with all the legendary equipment since there is no durability damage for their gear. So you end up feeling like a side character while your Thrall/Slave is this juggernaut tank with tiger tank plates for armor and hits like a howitzer. Just a poor feeling overall when I'm suppose to be the one pulling their chains.

Regardless of the negatives it was an enjoyable trek exploring the exiled lands. Lots to see and explore, interesting lore to uncover. If you are interested in exploration, story and Conan lore then I would grab it when on sale. Don't expect deep combat mechanics.

I think the game is good, but has a lot of issues. The update that added buildings and player construction pulling from storage is nice along side what seemed to be a decrease in needed distance between shrines, but that distance is still a problem and can cause an altar to be outside of your base also when constructing something and destroying it it's added to your inventory not back to the base's. speaking of constructing it can be finicky with where it allows you to place things, I had a long instance of trying to place a wall that for some reason wouldn't connect where i was pointing and always tried to be in front, behind, above or below where i wanted it and placing foundation on something can just not allow it for no reason. It also doesn't like if you try to connect two different sets of foundation, i.e. you tried to build a bridge with a friend and wanted to meet in the middle to shorten the work and it just doesn't connect so one of you has to demolish their side and you just continue from the other. It feels like you should wait until you're maxed level before doing any capturing stuff and with how the journey is set up you ultimately need to pretty much finish all of them before you can reset your character for the sake of building how you want that is if you bother with the journey. The journey system has it's own problems as it doesn't tick off later actions such as if you made a bedroll before even doing the beginning stuff it doesn't acknowledge it and you'll have to make it again when you get to it or when I tick the hide finish journeys I expect it to actually hide them not just move the scroll bar down, you know like how some appear after clearing one such as how finishing armorer unlocks the next level of armorer journeys just do that in reverse for finished ones when that option is ticked. Fighting against human enemies kinda just sucks as it's just whomever staggers the other first wins. Late game it feels very much like a mobile phone game where you just boot it up and the first hour is doing daily tasks around the base before moving on to actually play and while it's faster with friends it still doesn't change that aspect of the game. when knocked down it can be either immediately that you start getting up or it'll happen some time within the next three days, that is to say why does it randomly decide not to get up right away, I'm in the middle of combat. Isle of siptah kinda sucks, but I went over my issues with that in that dlc review. Again I feel that it is a good game, but it still needs a lot of work to make it a great game.

Fantastic game. I mean i could really just stop there, but i won't lol. This game has kept my attention every time i go to play it, usually each time i put in 50-100 hours just exploring and seeing what's new and to be honest... i still haven't done everything in the game.

I would for sure recommend this game if you like base building, exploring and fun combat. Be warned, there is a BIT of a story in this, but it does NOT hold your hand. You have to find it all yourself. There are no markers or waypoints or magic lines to guide you (save the ones you put down). They give you clues and SOMETIMES a picture drawn so you can look for landmarks to help you find it. Even with all of that, you will get lost just exploring, making new "friends" and building awesome bases.

Then when you get a base built you can do siege stuff. This is where you put a treasury down and npc enemies try to take your loot and that's just ONE of the endgame things. They are also dungeons, bosses and a whole other area to explore in Siptah. 

The co-op/multiplayer is also really fun. You are not tethered AT all to anyone else, so you could build a base on the far opposite side of the entire map with no problem and never see your friends again! (a bonus for some lol).

That said, if you do decide to get this game, i hope you have a fantastic time with it, and thanks for reading!

~Mystikos
